questions.question: If it rains, I _____ stay at home.
questions.explanation: First Conditional: If + present simple, will + base verb for real possibilities.

questions.question: If I had money, I _____ buy a car.
questions.explanation: Second Conditional: If + past simple, would + base verb for hypothetical situations.

questions.question: If she studies hard, she _____ pass the exam.
questions.explanation: First Conditional expresses a likely future result.

questions.question: If I were you, I _____ apologize.
questions.explanation: Second Conditional with 'If I were you' gives advice.

questions.question: They would travel if they _____ time.
questions.explanation: Second Conditional: past simple in the if-clause.

questions.question: If I _____ known about the meeting, I would have attended.
questions.explanation: Third Conditional: If + past perfect, would have + past participle for unreal past.

questions.question: She would have passed if she _____ harder.
questions.explanation: Third Conditional requires past perfect in the if-clause.

questions.question: If you heat ice, it _____.
questions.explanation: Zero Conditional: If + present, present for scientific facts and general truths.

questions.question: I would help you if I _____ how.
questions.explanation: Second Conditional: past simple 'knew' for hypothetical present situation.

questions.question: What would you do if you _____ a million dollars?
questions.explanation: Second Conditional asks about an imaginary situation.

questions.question: If he _____ earlier, he wouldn't have missed the train.
questions.explanation: Third Conditional: 'had left' (past perfect) for an unreal past condition.

questions.question: Had I known, I _____ helped you.
questions.explanation: Inverted Third Conditional: 'Had + subject + past participle' replaces 'If + subject + had + past participle'

questions.question: If only I _____ richer!
questions.explanation: 'If only' expresses a wish. 'Were' is used for all persons in formal English.

questions.question: Should you need any help, please _____ me.
questions.explanation: Inverted First Conditional: 'Should + subject + verb' replaces 'If + subject + should + verb'

questions.question: _____ it not for your help, I would have failed.
questions.explanation: Inverted Second Conditional: 'Were it not for' = 'If it were not for'

questions.question: If I _____ to warn you, you would have been in serious danger.
questions.explanation: Third Conditional negative: 'hadn't tried' for unreal past action.

questions.question: Mixed Conditional: If I had studied medicine, I _____ a doctor now.
questions.explanation: Mixed Conditional: past perfect in if-clause, would + base verb for present result of past condition.
